Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be finite nonempty sets. A **stochastic kernel**
from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$ is a matrix
$K=(K(y\mid x))_{x\in\mathcal X,y\in\mathcal Y}$ such that
$K(y\mid x)\ge0$ and $\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}K(y\mid x)=1$ for every
$x\in\mathcal X$. The convention is input first in the condition and output
first in the value $K(y\mid x)$.

For a probability vector $P=(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}$, the output vector
$PK$ on $\mathcal Y$ is
$$(PK)_y:=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xK(y\mid x).$$
It is a probability vector because its coordinates are nonnegative and
$\sum_y(PK)_y=\sum_xp_x\sum_yK(y\mid x)=\sum_xp_x=1$.

A **finite discrete memoryless channel (DMC)** is the channel sequence [[def-channel-sequence]] with fixed finite nonempty input and output alphabets $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ (with every subset measurable) and one stochastic kernel $W(y\mid x)$ from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$ ([[def-finite-stochastic-kernel]]). At every blocklength its input and output alphabets are $\mathcal X^n,\mathcal Y^n$, and its block kernel is
$$W^n(y^n\mid x^n):=\prod_{i=1}^n W(y_i\mid x_i).$$
Thus the same single-use transition law is applied independently at each coordinate, conditional on the input word. This page imposes no feedback or input-cost constraint.

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, with marginals $p_X(x):=\sum_y p_{XY}(x,y)$ and $p_Y(y):=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Define mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

where $D$ is the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and $(p_X\otimes p_Y)(x,y):=p_X(x)p_Y(y)$. Every ratio in the displayed sum is positive and finite: if $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$, then each marginal sum is at least that positive entry. The sum is over finite support, so $I(X;Y)$ is finite. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.

Write $\ln$ for the natural logarithm $\log$ of [[def-natural-logarithm]]. Unless a base is displayed, every information quantity on this page uses $\ln$ and is measured in **nats**. For a base $b>1$ and $t>0$, define
$$\log_b t:=\frac{\ln t}{\ln b}.$$
The denominator is positive: $b>1$, $\ln$ is strictly increasing, and $\ln 1=0$ by [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]. A base-$b$ entropy or divergence is obtained by replacing each $\ln$ in the finite formulas below by $\log_b$; use $0\log_b0:=0$ and assign $+\infty$ to a positive numerator over a zero denominator. The case $b=2$ measures **bits**; $b=e$ gives nats.

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

The real exponential function is $C^\infty$, and for every $m\in\mathbb N$,
$$\exp^{(m)}=\exp.$$
In particular $(\exp)'=\exp$.

Let $S$ be a finite sensitive variable and $X$ a finite useful variable with joint law $P_{SX}$. For each finite nonempty release alphabet $\mathcal Z$, choose a stochastic kernel $K(z\mid x)$ from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Z$ ([[def-finite-stochastic-kernel]]) and form

$$P_{SXZ}(s,x,z):=P_{SX}(s,x)K(z\mid x).$$

Thus the induced variables satisfy the explicitly defined factorization $P_{SXZ}=P_{SX}K_{Z\mid X}$, written $S-X-Z$. The **privacy–utility region** for this source is the closure in $\mathbb R^2$ of

$$\bigcup_{\mathcal Z,K}\left\{\bigl(I(S;Z),I(X;Z)\bigr)\right\},$$

where mutual information uses nats and the finite definition [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]]. The first coordinate is the chosen leakage metric and the second is the chosen retained-information utility. This model does not itself impose a distortion, rate, or perfect-privacy constraint; those define different optimization problems.

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, with marginals $p_X(x):=\sum_y p_{XY}(x,y)$ and $p_Y(y):=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. $$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

where $D$ is the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and $(p_X\otimes p_Y)(x,y):=p_X(x)p_Y(y)$. Every ratio in the displayed sum is positive and finite: if $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$, then each marginal sum is at least that positive entry. The sum is over finite support, so $I(X;Y)$ is finite. The conditional mixture in the Statement is therefore $P_Z(z)$, independent of $s$ for every $z$, in particular for every positive-mass $z$.

Conversely, assume the stated mixture is a constant $c_z$ in $s$ on $\operatorname{supp}P_S$ for each $z$ with $P_Z(z)>0$. Averaging it over $P_S$ shows $c_z=P_Z(z)$. Thus for every $s$ in the support and every $z$, $P_{Z\mid S=s}(z)=P_Z(z)$, so [F1] yields $P_{SZ}=P_S\otimes P_Z$.
Applying [F2] and [F3] to this equality gives $I(S;Z)=0$. This proves both directions, including zero-probability release symbols.

The encoder uses no feedback and the parties have no preshared secret key or forward public aid. The public code description is known to Eve, who observes $Z^n$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Define mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on the same set $[k]$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For a probability row vector $p$ on $[m]$ and a row vector $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iX_i$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

For every real $x\ge1$, the natural logarithm of
[[def-natural-logarithm]] satisfies
$$0\le\log x\le x-1\le x.$$

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, let $\mathbb{R}^n$ be the set of functions
$n \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on it
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). Then:

1. **Closed boxes are compact.** For reals $a_k \le b_k$ $(k < n)$ the box
   $Q = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_k \le x_k \le b_k \text{ for every } k < n \,\}$
   is a compact subset of $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ ([[def-metric-compactness]]).
2. **Heine-Borel.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ if and only if $K$ is closed in $\mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-topology]]) and bounded
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]).
3. **The real line.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}, d_{\mathbb{R}})$, the usual metric $d_{\mathbb{R}}(x,y) = |x-y|$
   ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]), if and only if $K$ is closed in
   $\mathbb{R}$ and bounded.

time and takes the **left** half whenever the left half still fails to be finitely
covered, the right half otherwise: a rule with two outcomes, decided by a
property of the box, not a selection. That is the whole reason the theorem is
available in ZF, while the general "complete and totally bounded implies compact"
([[thm-complete-and-totally-bounded-implies-compact]]) is not.

([[def-metric-continuity]]), $\mathbb{R}$ carrying its usual metric
$d_{\mathbb{R}}(s,t) = |s-t|$ ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]). Then the
image $f[X]$ is bounded above and below ([[def-bounded-set]]), and it has a
maximum and a minimum ([[def-max-min]]): there are points
$x_{\max}, x_{\min} \in X$ with

$$f(x_{\min}) \;\le\; f(x) \;\le\; f(x_{\max}) \qquad \text{for every } x \in X,$$

([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-infimum]]).

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

Let $X$ have a finite alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge1$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be any finite estimate output generated from $Y$, with an output alphabet that may contain symbols outside $\mathcal X$. Assume $X\to Y\to\widehat X$, and set $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$. Use $h_2$ as defined in [[thm-it-fano-inequality]]. Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln m.$$

If $X$ is uniform on $\mathcal X$, then

$$ (1-P_e)\ln m\le I(X;Y)+h_2(P_e).$$

Let $W(y\mid u)$ be a finite DMC and let $P_U$ be any fixed input probability vector. Let $P_Y(y)=\sum_uP_U(u)W(y\mid u)$. On the joint support $P_U(u)W(y\mid u)>0$, define

$$J(u,y):=\ln\frac{W(y\mid u)}{P_Y(y)},\qquad I:=I(U;Y),\qquad \sigma^2:=\sum_{u,y:P_U(u)W(y\mid u)>0}P_U(u)W(y\mid u)(J(u,y)-I)^2.$$

For IID pairs $(U_i,Y_i)\sim P_UW$, write $S_n=\sum_{i=1}^nJ(U_i,Y_i)$ and $B:=\max(0,\max_{P_U(u)W(y\mid u)>0}J(u,y))$. Then $J$ is bounded and $\mathbb E[J]=I$. For every $\delta>0$,

$$\Pr\left[\left|\frac{S_n}{n}-I\right|\ge\delta\right]\le\frac{\sigma^2}{n\delta^2}.$$

For every $\gamma>0$ there is a $\rho\in(0,1)$, depending only on $(P_U,W,\gamma)$, such that

$$\Pr[S_n>n(I+\gamma)]\le\rho^n.$$

Let $W(z\mid u)$ be a finite DMC, let $P_U$ be an input probability vector, and let $P_Z(z)=\sum_uP_U(u)W(z\mid u)$. On the joint support define $J(u,z):=\ln(W(z\mid u)/P_Z(z))$ and let $I=I(U;Z)$. Set $B=\max(0,\max_{P_U(u)W(z\mid u)>0}J(u,z))$. For $R_0>I$ and any $\gamma$ with $0<\gamma<R_0-I$, draw $L_n=\lceil e^{nR_0}\rceil$ independent words $U^n(\ell)\sim P_U^n$ and define the induced mixture

$$P_Z^n(z^n):=\prod_{i=1}^nP_Z(z_i),\qquad Q_{Z^n\mid C}:=\frac1{L_n}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L_n}W^n(\cdot\mid U^n(\ell)).$$

There is a $\rho\in(0,1)$, depending only on $(P_U,W,\gamma)$, for which

$$\mathbb E_C D(Q_{Z^n\mid C}\|P_Z^n)\le e^{-n(R_0-I-\gamma)}+(\ln2+nB)\rho^n,$$

and

$$\mathbb E_C\,\operatorname{TV}(Q_{Z^n\mid C},P_Z^n)\le\rho^n+\frac12e^{-n(R_0-I-\gamma)/2},$$

where $\operatorname{TV}(P,Q):=\frac12\sum_z|P(z)-Q(z)|$. Thus both expected deviations tend to zero. Here $D$ is the directional finite KL divergence of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]].

For every finite joint law $P_{UX}$ on a finite wiretap channel with input alphabet $\mathcal X$, where $U-X-(Y,Z)$ means $P_{UXYZ}(u,x,y,z)=P_{UX}(u,x)W(y,z\mid x)$, there is another finite auxiliary $\widetilde U$ with $|\widetilde{\mathcal U}|\le|\mathcal X|$ whose value of $I(\widetilde U;Y)-I(\widetilde U;Z)$ is at least $I(U;Y)-I(U;Z)$. Consequently

$$\sup_{P_{U,X}:\,U-X-(Y,Z)}[I(U;Y)-I(U;Z)]$$

is a maximum and may be restricted to $|\mathcal U|\le|\mathcal X|$. For each input law $q$, the single-letter objective $q\mapsto I_q(X;Y)-I_q(X;Z)$ is continuous on the finite probability simplex.

For finite nonempty alphabets $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y,\mathcal Z$, a stochastic kernel $W(y,z\mid x)$ from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z$, and every $n\ge1$, the block formula

$$W^n(y^n,z^n\mid x^n):=\prod_{i=1}^nW(y_i,z_i\mid x_i)$$

is a stochastic kernel from $\mathcal X^n$ to $(\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z)^n$.
For finite probability vectors $p,q$ on the same alphabet, $D(p\|q)\ge0$, and $D(p\|q)=0$ if and only if $p=q$. If $p_i>0=q_i$ for some coordinate, then $D(p\|q)=+\infty$.

derivations.claim: Let $C=C(W)$. A constant $U$ gives value zero, so $C\ge0$. By [F10] the maximum is attained with finite $|U|\le|X|$, and [F5] makes each mutual information finite, so $C<\infty$. For any fixed finite $P_{U,X}$, restrict $U$ to its positive-mass values and define the induced Bob and Eve channels $Q_Y(y\mid u):=\sum_xP_{X\mid U}(x\mid u)W_Y(y\mid x),\qquad Q_Z(z\mid u):=\sum_xP_{X\mid U}(x\mid u)W_Z(z\mid x).$ Each row sums to one because $P_{X\mid U=u}$ and the marginals $W_Y,W_Z$ are stochastic. These induced channels are finite DMCs, and their input-output mutual informations are $I(U;Y)$ and $I(U;Z)$.

Suppose $C>0$ and fix any $0\le R<C$. By [F10], choose a maximizing law $P_{U,X}$. Choose $R'$ with $R<R'<C$, then choose $R_0>I(U;Z)$ so that $R'+R_0<I(U;Y)$. Choose $\gamma_Y>0$ with $R'+R_0<I(U;Y)-\gamma_Y$. For each $n$, set $M_n=\lceil e^{nR'}\rceil$, $L_n=\lceil e^{nR_0}\rceil$, and independently draw $M_nL_n$ words $U^n(m,l)$ from $P_U^n$.

If $C=0$, the one-message code has zero error and zero leakage at every blocklength, so all four capacities are at least zero. In all cases, strong secrecy implies weak secrecy because [F5] and [F12] give $0\le I(M;Z^n)/n\le I(M;Z^n)$ for $n\ge1$; maximal error tending to zero implies average error tending to zero.

For the converse, consider any sequence of wiretap codes with average error $p_n\to0$ and weak leakage $\ell_n:=I(M;Z^n)$ satisfying $\ell_n/n\to0$. Fano's bound [F7] gives $ (1-p_n)\ln|\mathcal M_n|\le I(M;Y^n)+h_2(p_n)=I(M;Y^n)-I(M;Z^n)+\ell_n+h_2(p_n).$ The binary entropy is bounded by $\ln2$, since [F12] applied to $(p_n,1-p_n)$ and $(1/2,1/2)$ gives $0\le\ln2-h_2(p_n)$.

For $i=0,\ldots,n$, set $A_i:=I(M;Y^i,Z_{i+1}^n)$, with empty strings omitted, and set $V_i:=(Y^{i-1},Z_{i+1}^n)$. The mutual-information chain rule [F6] gives $I(M;Y^n)-I(M;Z^n)=A_n-A_0=\sum_{i=1}^n\left[I(M;Y_i\mid V_i)-I(M;Z_i\mid V_i)\right].$ Indeed, $A_i-A_{i-1}=I(M;Y_i\mid V_i)-I(M;Z_i\mid V_i)$ for each $i$, and the sum telescopes.

For a selected codebook, encode message $m$ by choosing $l$ uniformly and, conditional on $U^n(m,l)=u^n$, draw $X^n$ according to $$P_{X^n\mid U^n}(x^n\mid u^n)=\prod_{i=1}^nP_{X\mid U}(x_i\mid u_i),$$ using independent private draws at the coordinates. Thus the induced channels from $U$ to Bob and Eve are the finite DMCs $Q_Y(y\mid u):=\sum_xP_{X\mid U}(x\mid u)W_Y(y\mid x)$ and $Q_Z(z\mid u):=\sum_xP_{X\mid U}(x\mid u)W_Z(z\mid x)$, with block laws $Q_Y^n$ and $Q_Z^n$. For an output with $P_Y^n(y^n)=0$, declare erasure; it has probability zero because every sampled letter has positive $P_U$-mass and $P_Y(y)=\sum_uP_U(u)Q_Y(y\mid u)$. For an output with $P_Y^n(y^n)>0$, assign score $-\infty$ if $Q_Y^n(y^n\mid u^n)=0$ and otherwise use its log likelihood ratio. Decode the pair $(m,l)$ as the unique codeword satisfying $\ln\frac{Q_Y^n(Y^n\mid U^n(m,l))}{P_Y^n(Y^n)}>n\bigl(I(U;Y)-\gamma_Y\bigr)$; output its message coordinate $m$, and declare erasure if no unique pair passes. Under the transmitted pair, the missed-threshold probability is at most $\sigma_Y^2/(n\gamma_Y^2)$ by [F8]. For any incorrect pair, its independently drawn word is independent of the received $Y^n\sim P_Y^n$ under the random-code ensemble, and $\mathbb E_{U^n}[Q_Y^n(y^n\mid U^n)/P_Y^n(y^n)]=1$ on the support of $P_Y^n$. On the threshold event the likelihood ratio exceeds $e^{n(I(U;Y)-\gamma_Y)}$, so its indicator is bounded above by the ratio times $e^{-n(I(U;Y)-\gamma_Y)}$; taking expectations bounds the false-alarm probability by that exponential. If the true pair uniquely passes, the message is decoded correctly; hence message error is bounded by the missed-threshold event or the union of false-alarm events. The union bound over at most $M_nL_n-1$ incorrect pairs tends to zero: since $R',R_0\ge0$, $M_nL_n\le4e^{n(R'+R_0)}$, and $R'+R_0<I(U;Y)-\gamma_Y$. Thus the ensemble average message error tends to zero.

The code and channel law factor as $P_M(m)P_{X^n\mid M}(x^n\mid m)\prod_{j=1}^nW(y_j,z_j\mid x_j).$ In this finite sum, the time-$i$ factor $W(y_i,z_i\mid x_i)$ separates from all other coordinate factors. Therefore, after summing over the other inputs and outputs, $P(Y_i=y,Z_i=z\mid M=m,X_i=x,V_i=v)=W(y,z\mid x)$ whenever the conditioning event has positive probability. This proves $M-X_i-(Y_i,Z_i)$ conditional on each positive-mass $V_i=v$. Thus $P_{M,X_i\mid V_i=v}W$ is a finite auxiliary law allowed in the maximum defining $C$. By [F10], $I(M;Y_i\mid V_i=v)-I(M;Z_i\mid V_i=v)\le C.$ Average over positive-mass $v$ and sum over $i$ in step 1.5 to obtain $I(M;Y^n)-I(M;Z^n)\le nC$.

Use the same conditional product encoder law $P_{X^n\mid U^n}(x^n\mid u^n)=\prod_{i=1}^nP_{X\mid U}(x_i\mid u_i)$ with independent private coordinate draws as in step 2.1. Summing over $X^n$ through the product wiretap kernel gives the induced Eve DMC block law $Q_Z^n(z^n\mid u^n)=\prod_{i=1}^nQ_Z(z_i\mid u_i)$, where $Q_Z(z\mid u)=\sum_xP_{X\mid U}(x\mid u)W_Z(z\mid x)$. Eve's conditional output law for message $m$ is the mixture of the $L_n$ induced $Q_Z^n(\cdot\mid U^n(m,l))$ outputs. Let $d(\mathcal C)$ be the average over $m$ of its KL divergence from $P_Z^n$. For each fixed $m$, its randomization subcode has exactly the IID codebook law in [F9], so $\mathbb E_{\mathcal C}d(\mathcal C)\to0$. Let $a(\mathcal C)$ be the codebook's average Bob error. Step 2.1 and finite averaging give $\mathbb E_{\mathcal C}a(\mathcal C)\to0$. Fix an ordering of the finite auxiliary alphabet and order its finite word/codebook sets lexicographically. At each $n$, take the first codebook whose $a(\mathcal C_n)+d(\mathcal C_n)$ is no larger than its finite ensemble mean. Such a codebook exists by finite averaging, so this specifies a sequence with $a(\mathcal C_n)+d(\mathcal C_n)\to0$ without countable choices.

Write $\eta_n=a(\mathcal C_n)+d(\mathcal C_n)$ and, for each message $m$, write $e_m$ for its Bob error and $d_m=D(P_{Z^n\mid m,\mathcal C_n}\|P_Z^n)$. Delete every message with $e_m>t_n$ or $d_m>t_n$, where $t_n=\sqrt{\eta_n}+1/n$. For each message, $\mathbf1\{e_m>t_n\text{ or }d_m>t_n\}\le(e_m+d_m)/t_n$; averaging over the uniform message bounds the deleted fraction by $\eta_n/t_n\le\sqrt{\eta_n}$. Thus for all sufficiently large $n$ the retained fraction tends to one and is positive, and each retained message has both $e_m,d_m\le t_n\to0$. Restrict the encoder to retained messages and map any old decoder output outside the retained set to erasure; this cannot increase the error for a retained message. For the finitely many earlier blocklengths use a one-message code.

For the uniform message on the retained set $S_n$, put $\bar P_{Z^n}=|S_n|^{-1}\sum_{m\in S_n}P_{Z^n\mid m,\mathcal C_n}$. Expanding the finite KL sums and grouping terms gives the exact identity $\frac1{|S_n|}\sum_{m\in S_n}D(P_{Z^n\mid m,\mathcal C_n}\|P_Z^n)=\frac1{|S_n|}\sum_{m,z^n:P_{Z^n\mid m,\mathcal C_n}(z^n)>0}P_{Z^n\mid m,\mathcal C_n}(z^n)\ln\frac{P_{Z^n\mid m,\mathcal C_n}(z^n)}{P_Z^n(z^n)}=\frac1{|S_n|}\sum_{m,z^n:P_{Z^n\mid m,\mathcal C_n}(z^n)>0}P_{Z^n\mid m,\mathcal C_n}(z^n)\ln\frac{P_{Z^n\mid m,\mathcal C_n}(z^n)}{\bar P_{Z^n}(z^n)}+\sum_{z^n:\bar P_{Z^n}(z^n)>0}\bar P_{Z^n}(z^n)\ln\frac{\bar P_{Z^n}(z^n)}{P_Z^n(z^n)}=I(M;Z^n)+D(\bar P_{Z^n}\|P_Z^n).$ The reference law has positive mass wherever any induced Eve output has positive mass, so all terms are finite. By [F12], $I(M;Z^n)\le |S_n|^{-1}\sum_{m\in S_n}d_m\le t_n\to0$. Also $|S_n|\ge(1-\sqrt{\eta_n})M_n$ and $M_n\ge e^{nR'}$, while $n^{-1}\ln(1-\sqrt{\eta_n})\to0$; hence $\liminf_n n^{-1}\ln|S_n|\ge R'$. This constructs a maximal-error, strong-secrecy sequence at rate at least $R'$, and therefore every $R<C$ is achievable for all four criteria.

Substitute step 2.2 into step 1.4, divide by $n(1-p_n)$, and use $p_n\to0$, $\ell_n/n\to0$, and $0\le h_2(p_n)\le\ln2$ to get $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln|\mathcal M_n|\le C$. This converse applies to weak secrecy and average error; it also bounds strong-secrecy or maximal-error sequences because each implies the corresponding weaker condition. Together with the achievability and zero-capacity branches, all four operational capacities equal $C(W)$.

citations.quote:
A finite wiretap channel [[def-it-wiretap-channel]] is **degraded from Bob to Eve** if there is a finite stochastic kernel $V(z\mid y)$ from Bob's output alphabet to Eve's output alphabet such that

$$W(y,z\mid x)=W_Y(y\mid x)V(z\mid y)\quad\text{for every }x,y,z.$$

Equivalently, for every input law $P_X$, the induced joint law is $P_X(x)W_Y(y\mid x)V(z\mid y)$. The requirement specifies the joint coupling of Bob's and Eve's outputs, not only their separate marginal channels.

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, with marginals $p_X(x):=\sum_y p_{XY}(x,y)$ and $p_Y(y):=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Define mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

where $D$ is the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and $(p_X\otimes p_Y)(x,y):=p_X(x)p_Y(y)$. Every ratio in the displayed sum is positive and finite: if $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$, then each marginal sum is at least that positive entry. The sum is over finite support, so $I(X;Y)$ is finite. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

Let $X,Y,Z$ have a joint pmf on finite alphabets and suppose that, for every $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$,

$$p_{XZ|y}(x,z)=p_{X|y}(x)p_{Z|y}(z).$$

This is the finite Markov condition $X\to Y\to Z$. Then

$$I(X;Z)\le I(X;Y),$$

with equality if and only if $I(X;Y|Z)=0$, equivalently $X$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given every positive-mass value of $Z$.

For every finite joint law $P_{UX}$ on a finite wiretap channel with input alphabet $\mathcal X$, where $U-X-(Y,Z)$ means $P_{UXYZ}(u,x,y,z)=P_{UX}(u,x)W(y,z\mid x)$, there is another finite auxiliary $\widetilde U$ with $|\widetilde{\mathcal U}|\le|\mathcal X|$ whose value of $I(\widetilde U;Y)-I(\widetilde U;Z)$ is at least $I(U;Y)-I(U;Z)$. Consequently

$$\sup_{P_{U,X}:\,U-X-(Y,Z)}[I(U;Y)-I(U;Z)]$$

is a maximum and may be restricted to $|\mathcal U|\le|\mathcal X|$. For each input law $q$, the single-letter objective $q\mapsto I_q(X;Y)-I_q(X;Z)$ is continuous on the finite probability simplex.

Let $W(y,z\mid x)$ be a finite wiretap DMC as in [[def-it-wiretap-channel]], with no input-cost constraint, feedback, or preshared secret key. Let

$$C(W):=\max_{\substack{\mathcal U\text{ finite},\ P_{U,X}:\ U-X-(Y,Z)}}\bigl[I(U;Y)-I(U;Z)\bigr],$$

where $U-X-(Y,Z)$ means the joint law factors as $P_U(u)P_{X\mid U}(x\mid u)W(y,z\mid x)$. The maximum is attained with $|\mathcal U|\le|\mathcal X|$. The four capacities defined in [[def-it-wiretap-secrecy-capacities]] are equal:

$$C_{\mathrm{av,weak}}=C_{\mathrm{av,strong}}=C_{\mathrm{max,weak}}=C_{\mathrm{max,strong}}=C(W).$$

Fix an error criterion $e\in\{\mathrm{av},\mathrm{max}\}$ and a secrecy criterion $s\in\{\mathrm{weak},\mathrm{strong}\}$. For each code let $P_{\rm err}^{(n)}=P_{e,\rm av}^{(n)}$ when $e=\mathrm{av}$ and $P_{\rm err}^{(n)}=P_{e,\rm max}^{(n)}$ when $e=\mathrm{max}$. A rate $R\ge0$ in nats per channel use is $(e,s)$-achievable for a finite wiretap channel [[def-it-wiretap-channel]] if there is a sequence of wiretap codes, one at each blocklength $n\ge1$, such that

$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\ln|\mathcal M_n|\ge R,\qquad P_{\rm err}^{(n)}\longrightarrow0,$$

and the sequence satisfies secrecy criterion $s$ from [[def-it-weak-and-strong-secrecy]], with leakage measured by [[def-it-information-leakage-and-equivocation]]. Define $C_{e,s}$ as the supremum of all such rates. Thus this definition gives four operational capacities, distinguished by average or maximal error and weak or strong secrecy.

derivations.claim: Fix any finite $P_{U,X}$ and form the joint law $P_{U,X,Y,Z}(u,x,y,z)=P_{U,X}(u,x)W(y,z\mid x)$, which is the notation $U-X-(Y,Z)$. For each $u$ with $P_U(u)>0$, the degraded factorization [F1] makes $X-Y-Z$ under the posterior law $P_{X\mid U=u}$, so [F4] gives $I(X;Z\mid U=u)\le I(X;Y\mid U=u)$. Averaging over $u$ yields $I(X;Z\mid U)\le I(X;Y\mid U)$.

Conversely, for any input law $P_X$, take $U=X$. Then $U-X-(Y,Z)$ holds and $I(U;Y)-I(U;Z)=I(X;Y)-I(X;Z)$. Thus the supremum over auxiliaries is at least the supremum of the displayed single-letter objective.

The Markov condition $U-X-Y$ gives $I(U;Y\mid X)=0$, so the chain rule [F3] yields $I(X;Y)=I(U;Y)+I(X;Y\mid U)$. Likewise $U-X-Z$ gives $I(X;Z)=I(U;Z)+I(X;Z\mid U)$. Subtracting these identities and using step 1.1 shows $I(U;Y)-I(U;Z)=I(X;Y)-I(X;Z)-\bigl(I(X;Y\mid U)-I(X;Z\mid U)\bigr)\le I(X;Y)-I(X;Z).$

By [F5], choose an auxiliary law attaining the maximum in the general formula. Step 2.1 shows that replacing this law by $U=X$ at the same marginal $P_X$ cannot decrease its value, so this input law attains the maximum of the single-letter expression. Every input law is itself an allowed auxiliary with $U=X$ by step 1.2. Thus the auxiliary maximum equals the displayed maximum, and [F6] identifies it with all four capacities in the sense of [F7].
